title: Alleviate token-velocity oscillation and background warmup causing cross-deployment throughput collapse
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary:
Customers have reported intermittent collapses in tokens/sec and TTFT spikes across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments for batches that fan out to heterogeneous model variants. The failure mode presents as a 10-60s tail where first-token latency climbs and sustained tokens/sec drops by 40-70% for affected requests.

Observable pattern and hypothesis:
- On surge traffic we observe the background warmup scheduler deferring primer requests for models that are in a 'low-priority' warmup bucket.
- Deferred priming accumulates unseen KV-cache misses and a compacted priming wave is released once warmup budget reopens, producing a token-velocity oscillation: a short high-velocity phase followed by eviction pressure and forced kernel-context-switches.
- Eviction pulses and kernel reselection coincide with large fanout requests (multi-variant routing) and with certain quantized kernel code paths (int8 microkernels).
- The oscillation amplifies when autoscaler and shedder interact: autoscaler briefly increases capacity reacting to the high-velocity phase while shedder triggers back-off during the low phase, creating throughput collapse.

Impact matrix:
- Hosted: Multiple paying customers reported degraded RT and increased error budgets.
- Dedicated: Reserved pools experienced prolonged throughput drops causing SLA alerts.
- Private: VPC customers saw long-tail TTFT spikes correlated with warmup/eviction events; root-cause traces show identical scheduler heuristics.

Immediate mitigation applied (done):
- Temporarily pinned warmup quotas to avoid aggressive deferral for affected customer routes (Host/ Dedicated / Private) — rolled as a targeted config patch (console rollout id: rollout/142403-temp-pin).
- Deployed a rate-ladder throttle in the request router to smooth priming fanout for the highest-fanout routes (controlled threshold = 6 variants).
- Enabled an emergency eviction-smoothing flag to increase KV-cache grace window from 2s -> 8s for int8 kernels on the affected fleet (config flag: runtime.eviction.grace_ms).
These mitigations reduced immediate TTFT spikes for impacted customers by ~60% while we iterate on a long-term fix.

Investigation tasks (in-flight):
1) Instrument warmup scheduler internals and trace bucket lifecycle end-to-end for a single request across routing -> scheduler -> kernel selection (owner: Aisha).
2) Reproduce oscillation in staging by replaying production traces with controlled fanout and mixed quant kernels (owner: Priya).
3) Evaluate kernel-selection hysteresis: keep previous kernel for X requests when a small context-change is detected to reduce churn (owner: Marco).
4) Quantize and compare eviction policies: test grace-window vs. token-budget windows and measure tokens/sec and TTFT under load (owner: Aisha).
5) Autoscaler-shedder coupling audit: identify feedback loops causing overreaction to short spikes (owner: Jen).

Proposed long-term fix (design sketched):
- Introduce a windowed-rate-shepherd that smooths primer issuance: primers are rate-limited in laddered buckets (fast/medium/slow) and promoted deterministically rather than being deferred wholesale.
- Add kernel-hysteresis so kernel reselection requires sustained telemetry delta across a sliding window (default 12s) to avoid oscillatory reselections during transient bursts.
- Make warmup scheduling preemptible only at defined safe points (post-kv-priming) to avoid leaving partially-primed requests that later produce synchronized bursts.
- Provide a per-customer warmup policy override accessible from Console for enterprise customers with high fanout or strict SLOs.

Acceptance criteria for rollout-1:
- No more than 10% degradation from baseline tokens/sec in controlled stress tests for workloads that previously produced collapse.
- TTFT P95 regression <= 10% vs baseline in canary region for 48h.
- Console exposes warmup-policy toggle for enterprise customers and default policy set to laddered-shepherd.

Artifacts and links:
- Playback trace used for staging reproduction: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/trace/plays/142403-repro
- Canary dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/canaries/runtime-1.22/142403
- PR with emergency pin and router throttles: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/14812
- Design doc for laddered warmup and kernel hysteresis: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Laddered+Warmup+Design

Next steps and timeline:
- 2026-03-15: complete instrumentation and repro (status: in progress).
- 2026-03-16: land kernel-hysteresis prototype behind feature flag and run limited canary.
- 2026-03-17: evaluate autoscaler-shedder changes and tune thresholds.
- 2026-03-18: if canary metrics pass, rollout laddered-shepherd and make console toggle available.

Postmortem notes to draft after resolution:
- Exact root cause correlation between int8 kernel eviction cascade and warmup deferral latency.
- Role of autoscaler reaction window parameters and shedder sensitivity.
- Recommendations for default warmup policies per deployment mode.
